title: Nord USB device catalog
description: Cross-language (Python + Kotlin) source of truth for per-instrument USB/protocol constants. See devices/README.md for how to add a new instrument, and docs/PROTOCOLS.md §8 for the reverse-engineered protocol these values come from.

schemaVersion.description: Bump only on a breaking change to this shape. New optional fields with safe defaults don't need a bump.

contentVersionScales.description: Content tag -> divisor for that tag's content-version field (docs/PROTOCOLS.md §3.5). Only the exceptions are listed; anything absent uses the default of 100, e.g. 312 -> '3.12'. Keyed by content tag rather than nested per device because tags are globally unique across instruments (docs/PROTOCOLS.md §8.9's naming rule). The Stage 2 EX's own tags are unscaled, measured for ns2p/ns2s and assumed for ns2l/ns2y.

programCategories.description: The master preset-category-tag catalog, id -> name (docs/PROTOCOLS.md §3.3.4.1). This is Clavia's own list, shared across the whole Nord product line, 54 ids (0-53). No instrument implements all of it: each device entry picks its own subset via 'programCategoryIds'. Keyed by id rather than by name because the master list is not injective - ids 2 and 37 are both 'Wind', 14 and 43 both 'User' - so a name -> id map cannot represent it.

sampleCategories.description: The master sample-category catalog (docs/PROTOCOLS.md §3.5.1.1), keyed by main-category id 0-18. Clavia's own list, shared across the product line like 'programCategories'. An 'nsmp' item record's tag-specific field is a (main, sub) pair: the high half indexes this map, the low half indexes that entry's 'subCategories'. A sub-category of "" means the item has none, which is index 0 for every category except 'Synth' - the one that uses index 0 as a real name.

short.description: Abbreviation the instrument's own display uses, e.g. 'Accord/Harm'. Equal to 'name' where no abbreviation was needed.

subCategories.description: Sub-category id -> name, complete including index 0.

id.description: Stable machine id, e.g. 'nord_grand'. Not currently read by either app, but a device needs one so profiles can be referenced (test fixtures, future tooling) without depending on array order.

name.description: Human-readable name shown to the user, e.g. 'Nord Grand'.

maxBankLetter.description: Last valid bank letter for preset ids, e.g. 'P' or 'D' (docs/PROTOCOLS.md §3.3.2).

maxGroup.description: Last valid group number for preset ids.

slotsPerGroup.description: Slots per group - the divisor used to translate group/slot into a flat item index.

maxDisplayTextLen.description: Character width of the instrument's status-message display (docs/PROTOCOLS.md §3.2).

maxProgramNameLen.description: Longest program name the instrument actually stores (docs/PROTOCOLS.md §3.3.4). Measured, not guessed: an oversized SET_NAME is accepted with status 0 and the instrument silently keeps this many characters. Separate from maxDisplayTextLen even though both are 16 on every instrument measured so far - they are different limits that happen to coincide, and conflating them would hide the day one of them moves.

supportedFirmwareVersions.description: Firmware version codes (as returned by the bRequest=4 control transfer, e.g. 168 for '1.68') this profile has been verified against. An empty array means 'skip the firmware check' - used for a device nobody has captured yet, not for a real supported instrument.

programCategoryIds.description: Which ids of the top-level programCategories master list this instrument actually offers - an index into it, not a redefinition of it (docs/PROTOCOLS.md §3.3.4.1). The Nord Grand and Stage 2 EX offer the identical 21. Optional: omitting it (or null) means 'this instrument's subset has not been established', which resolves to no known names at all, so --set-program-category will reject every name rather than guess. Unlike every other per-device value here it cannot be read off the instrument: the wire only ever carries the numeric id.

programCategoryNameOverrides.description: Ids from 'programCategoryIds' that this instrument displays under a different name than the master list gives them, id -> name. Both current instruments relabel 23/24 ('EPiano'/'Wurl' in the master list) as 'EPiano1'/'EPiano2'. An id here that is absent from 'programCategoryIds' is ignored.
